You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

def solve(g):
    g=[r[:] for r in g]
    H,W=len(g),len(g[0])
    # find pattern: largest connected nonzero component (exclude isolated dots of the noise color? assume dots are the single non-pattern cells)
    cells=[(r,c) for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if g[r][c]!=0]
    cs=set(cells)
    def comps():
        seen=set(); out=[]
        for p in cells:
            if p in seen: continue
            st=[p]; comp=set()
            while st:
                r,c=st.pop()
                if (r,c) in seen: continue
                seen.add((r,c)); comp.add((r,c))
                for dr,dc in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                    q=(r+dr,c+dc)
                    if q in cs and q not in seen: st.append(q)
            out.append(comp)
        return out
    comps=list(comps())
    comps.sort(key=len, reverse=True)
    pat=max(comps,key=len)  # pattern = largest comp
    dots=[p for p in cells if p not in set(pat)]
    rs=[p[0] for p in pat]; cs_=[p[1] for p in pat]
    r0,r1,c0,c1=min(rs),max(rs),min(cs_),max(cs_)
    h=r1-r0+1; w=c1-c0+1
    pt=[[g[r][c] for c in range(c0,c1+1)] for r in range(r0,r1+1)]
    res=[row[:] for row in g]
    for (r,c) in dots:
        orr=r-h//2; occ=c-w//2
        for i in range(h):
            for j in range(w):
                rr,cc=orr+i,occ+j
                if 0<=rr<H and 0<=cc<W: res[rr][cc]=pt[i][j]
    return res

# - Isolated single-cell "noise" markers (color 5) indicate copy locations.

import json
def f(g):
    g=[r[:] for r in g]; H,W=len(g),len(g[0])
    seen=set(); nz={(r,c) for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if g[r][c]!=0}
    comps=[]
    for p in nz:
        if p in seen: continue
        st=[p]; comp=set()
        while st:
            r,c=st.pop()
            if (r,c) in seen: continue
            seen.add((r,c)); comp.add((r,c))
            for dr,dc in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                q=(r+dr,c+dc)
                if q in nz and q not in seen: st.append(q)
        comps.append(comp)
    comps.sort(key=len)
    pat=comps[-1]          # largest = the pattern object
    dots=[c.pop() for c in comps[:-1]]  # every other comp is a stray marker
    rs=[x[0] for x in pat]; cs_=[x[1] for x in pat]
    r0,r1,c0,c1=min(rs),max(rs),min(cs_),max(cs_)
    h=r1-r0+1; w=c1-c0+1
    pt=[[g[r][c] for c in range(c0,c1+1)] for r in range(r0,r1+1)]
    res=[row[:] for row in g]
    for (r,c) in dots:
        orr=r-h//2; occ=c-w//2
        for i in range(h):
            for j in range(w):
                rr,cc=orr+i,occ+j
                if 0<=rr<H and 0<=cc<W and pt[i][j]!=0:
                    res[rr][cc]=pt[i][j]
    return res

# Quick verification of current best hypothesis before requesting a second demo:
# Rule A: copy the largest connected nonzero object (the pattern) onto every isolated stray cell,
# centered on the stray cell (top-left = dot - (h//2, w//2)), copying only nonzero cells.
def f(g):
    g=[r[:] for r in g]; H,W=len(g),len(g[0])
    seen=set(); nz={(r,c) for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if g[r][c]!=0}; comps=[]
    for p in nz:
        if p in seen: continue
        st=[p]; comp=set()
        while st:
            r,c=st.pop()
            if (r,c) in seen: continue
            seen.add((r,c)); comp.add((r,c))
            for dr,dc in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                q=(r+dr,c+dc)
                if q in nz and q not in seen: st.append(q)
        comps.append(comp)
    comps.sort(key=len)
    pat=comps[-1]; dots=[c.pop() for c in comps[:-1]]
    rs=[x[0] for x in pat]; cs_=[x[1] for x in pat]
    r0,r1,c0,c1=min(rs),max(rs),min(cs_),max(cs_)
    pt=[[g[r][c] for c in range(c0,c1+1)] for r in range(r0,r1+1)]; h=r1-r0+1; w=c1-c0+1
    res=[row[:] for row in g]
    for (r,c) in dots:
        orr=r-h//2; occ=c-w//2
        for i in range(h):
            for j in range(w):
                rr,cc=orr+i,occ+j
                if 0<=rr<H and 0<=cc<W and pt[i][j]!=0: res[rr][cc]=pt[i][j]
    return res
import json
